clue.text: Pandemonium in game briefly

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the name of the game loses its final letter

parts.note: rackets is a court game played with a hard ball, ancestor of squash

explanation.surface: A sports match descends into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A din or uproarious commotion is a racket, a near synonym for wild noisy disorder.

clue.text: Be sufficient for trip to get Manx cat

indicators.note: a Manx cat is famously tailless, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a run is a short journey
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Wondering whether there's enough money for a trip to buy a cat from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: Manx cats come from the Isle of Man and are born without tails.
explanation.definitionFit: If funds run to something they are enough to cover it, an idiom for being adequate.

clue.text: Ancient region's prince died in church near Assyria's capital

indicators.note: near means next to, so the last piece is set alongside
being in something means sitting inside it, so the prince and the death go inside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare
D is the standard abbreviation for died

indicators.note: a capital is the head letter of a word, so only the opening one is used

parts.note: opening letter of Assyria

explanation.surface: An ancient prince dies in a church close to the Assyrian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaldea was a land in southern Mesopotamia in antiquity, home to the Chaldean dynasty of Babylon.

clue.text: Be interested in record set by piebald horse needing no introduction

indicators.note: an introduction comes first, so without it the opening letter is dropped
one thing set by another is placed beside it, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: to enter data is to record it
a pinto is a horse with patchy markings

explanation.surface: A record time set by a famous patchy horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing no introduction' sounds like praise for a famous horse, but it means removing its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter into something is to take part in it with enthusiasm, showing real engagement.

clue.text: Plaster head of saint, mysterious on reflection, student ignored

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: opening letter of saint

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the word for mysterious is read from right to left
something ignored is left out, so the letter for the student is dropped

parts.note: occult means hidden or mysterious
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A plaster bust of a saint, eerily facing away, which the student has passed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plaster head' looks like one phrase, a cast bust, but the definition is just the first word. L for student comes from the learner-driver plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a type of fine plaster or render used for coating walls and mouldings.

clue.text: Support holding captive as bait

indicators.note: a captor holds a prisoner inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prop keeping a hostage, used as a lure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a link to the definition but is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To bait someone is to taunt or provoke them, which is what teasing does.

clue.text: Around the beginning of April replacing one ship's framework

indicators.note: replacing means one letter takes another's place in the word

parts.note: circa is Latin for around, used with dates

indicators.note: a beginning is the opening of a word, so its first letter is used

parts.note: opening letter of April
I is the Roman numeral one
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Around the start of April a ship's frame is swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal but supplies CIRCA, whose I becomes A.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcass can mean the skeleton or structural shell of a building or ship.

clue.text: Troubled throne to face battles essentially one after the other

indicators.note: facing something means standing next to it, so the pieces are set side by side
something troubled is disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the essence is the heart, so the central letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the central letter of battles

explanation.surface: A shaky monarchy faces a string of wars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the trot' is British informal for in succession, as in three wins on the trot.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means consecutively or in a row, describing things happening in succession.

clue.text: Dig up a French article on cunning Hungarian leader

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing put on another simply comes after it in the line

parts.note: une is the French feminine indefinite article, meaning a
art can mean craft or guile

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: opening letter of Hungarian

explanation.surface: Someone digs up a French object belonging to a crafty leader from Hungary.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is literally to excavate it from the ground, a straightforward synonym for exhume.

clue.text: Tell fled heading west at speed

indicators.note: across clues read left to right, so heading west means going right to left

parts.note: ran away means fled
a speed is a rate, as in going at a great rate

explanation.surface: An instruction to report someone who escaped westwards very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to recount or relate a story, which is what telling one involves.

clue.text: Lie mostly over hankering at first for tosser seen on farm

indicators.note: lying over something covers it, so one piece wraps the others
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a porky is a lie, from rhyming slang porky pie
an itch is a craving

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: opening letter of for

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a farmyard idiot who fibs and yearns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tosser' is British slang for a fool, but here it is something that tosses hay. A porky (pie) is rhyming slang for a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitchfork is a long-handled farm tool used to toss hay and straw.

clue.text: Course of action following marches only just acceptable

indicators.note: the course of action comes after, so it is placed second in the line

parts.note: marches are frontier lands, as in the Welsh Marches
a line is a policy or approach, as in taking a hard line

explanation.surface: A plan made after political protests is barely passable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marches' suggests demonstrations, but here it means border regions, as with the Welsh Marches between England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Something borderline sits right on the edge between passable and unacceptable, so it barely scrapes through.

clue.text: Consented to get rid of soldiers advanced in years

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, so those letters drop out of the word

parts.note: agreed means consented
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to dismiss elderly troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged describes a person who is old, having lived a great many years.

clue.text: Make Native American give up drugs after last of warnings

indicators.note: the tribe name comes after, so it is placed second
the last of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: final letter of warnings

indicators.note: giving up a habit means dropping it, so the drug letters are removed

parts.note: the Pawnee are a Native American people of the Great Plains
E is ecstasy, so two Es for plural drugs

explanation.surface: A warning to a Native American to quit using drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To spawn is to produce or generate, especially offspring, so it can stand for make.

clue.text: Combination of circumstances making yours truly stressed about living in Swiss town

indicators.note: someone living in a town is inside it, so these letters go inside the town's name

parts.note: Sion is the capital of the Swiss canton of Valais
yours truly means me, the writer

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word for stressed is read backwards

parts.note: taut means tense or strained

explanation.surface: Circumstances that make the writer anxious about living in a Swiss town.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation is the set of conditions or state of affairs prevailing at a given time.

clue.text: Arrogant nonsense to take legal action against boxing trainer ultimately

parts.note: cock is slang for nonsense, as in poppycock

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing in a box, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: to sue is to bring a lawsuit

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: final letter of trainer

explanation.surface: A cocky boxer threatens to sue his trainer over some rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocksure describes someone overconfident and presumptuous, a close synonym for haughty self-assurance.

clue.text: Gallant in good spirits catches sound daughter missed

indicators.note: catching something means holding it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: cheer is a cheerful mood, as in being of good cheer

indicators.note: something missed is absent, so the daughter's letter is left out

parts.note: a sound argument is a valid one
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A cheerful gentleman hears something but his daughter is absent.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevalier is a knight or a courteous gentleman, exactly what a gallant is.

clue.text: Initiate rule about books framed by teachers in school

indicators.note: a picture framed by something is surrounded by it, so the teachers' word goes round

parts.note: the teaching body of a school is its staff
R is an abbreviation for rule

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the books abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: School teachers launch a rule concerning books.
explanation.definitionFit: To start off is to begin or set going, so it works as a synonym for launching or initiating.

clue.text: Retrieve data from computer reportedly found in temporary fortification

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken or heard, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: to read out data is to retrieve it from memory or storage

explanation.surface: A soldier recovering files from a laptop inside a makeshift fort.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a small enclosed fieldwork, often hastily built, a defensive military outpost.

clue.text: Use effectively with skilful removal of pressure

indicators.note: removal takes something away, so one letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: expert means highly skilled
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Applying expertise to relieve stress.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert influence or strength is to bring it to bear forcefully, putting it into effective use.

clue.text: Far from moderate constituents of Rex meet

indicators.note: constituents are the parts making something up, so the letters are treated as loose material to rebuild

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Voters in a constituency meet a king, Rex, and they are hardly moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means radical or immoderate, the opposite of middle-of-the-road views.

clue.text: Prevented from speaking with poet

indicators.note: taking a word from speaking means going by how it is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: barred means prevented or blocked

explanation.surface: Someone is silenced alongside a poet, as if banned from speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prevented from speaking' reads as gagged, but the last two words signal a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a traditional term for a poet, Shakespeare being known as the Bard.

clue.text: Commercial enterprise initially involved in spurious rent claim

indicators.note: being involved in something makes that letter part of the group that gets jumbled
spurious means false, so the letters are a fake arrangement to be rearranged
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of enterprise is used

parts.note: opening letter of enterprise
taken as written

explanation.surface: A business firm is caught up in a bogus rent demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile relates to merchants and trade, so it is a fitting adjective for anything business-related.

clue.text: Frantically busy FBI agent not good in charge

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for good is taken away

parts.note: a G-man is a US government agent, especially of the FBI
G is the abbreviation for good
IC means in charge

explanation.surface: A frazzled FBI agent, not up to the job, is in command.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic describes wild, frenzied activity, as of someone rushed off their feet.

clue.text: Attended by good fortune gutsy Penny fled

indicators.note: something that has fled has gone, so the penny letter disappears

parts.note: plucky means brave and spirited
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A brave woman named Penny runs away with good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lucky means being favoured by chance, having fortune on your side.

clue.text: Stimulating for oddly prim fashion designer perhaps

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, so the first and third letters are kept

parts.note: odd letters of prim
Mary Quant was the British designer credited with popularising the miniskirt

explanation.surface: A prim fashion designer finds something exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' warns that the designer is just one example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquant means pleasantly sharp or stimulating, used of flavours and of intriguing ideas.

clue.text: The rest is for Hamlet to put a stop to

definitions.meaning: first meaning: completing Hamlet's dying line in Shakespeare's play
second meaning: to quieten or suppress

explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's final words are 'The rest is silence', so the missing word is the answer; 'rest' also teases the musical pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's last line ends with this word, and as a verb it means to suppress or make quiet.

clue.text: Time allowed for preparation of literary review

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a short critical write-up of a book or play

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a single phrase about preparing a review; it splits at 'of' into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means advance warning given before an event, and also a brief published critique of a book.

clue.text: Not under the control of another female dance company finally

definitions.text: Not under the control of another

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
a reel is a lively Scottish folk dance

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so the closing letter of company is taken

parts.note: final letter of company

explanation.surface: A woman dancing with a troupe, independent of anyone's direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting freely means acting independently, without being directed or constrained by someone else.
